meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 13: Extensions
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: Your client polls tasks/get and wants to stop polling as soon as the status can no longer change. Which statuses mean it can stop?

options.text: completed and failed only, since a cancelled task may still finish
completed only, because failed and cancelled tasks are retried automatically
completed, failed and cancelled: once reached, the state does not change
completed, failed, cancelled and input_required

questions.explanation: working and input_required are transient; completed, failed and cancelled are terminal. Cancellation is cooperative, so a cancelled request may still end up completed or failed, but once a terminal state is reached the task does not change again.

questions.question: Which set of task methods exists in the 2026-07-28 Tasks extension?

options.text: tasks/get, tasks/update, tasks/cancel
tasks/create, tasks/poll, tasks/cancel
tasks/get, tasks/result, tasks/cancel
tasks/get, tasks/list, tasks/result

questions.explanation: The redesign replaced the blocking tasks/result with polling via tasks/get, added tasks/update for client-to-server input, and removed tasks/list. Tasks are created by the server returning a CreateTaskResult, not by a tasks/create call.

questions.question: Which identifier format do official MCP extensions use, and where do they live?

options.text: A reverse-DNS name owned by the implementing vendor, such as com.acme/tasks
A semantic version string such as tasks@1.2.0, kept in the main specification repository itself
A bare name such as tasks, registered in the MCP Registry
A vendor prefix plus name, such as io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks, in ext-* repositories

questions.explanation: Extension identifiers follow the _meta key rules with a mandatory prefix; official ones use the io.modelcontextprotocol prefix and live in repositories prefixed ext- (experimental ones in experimental-ext-). Third parties use a reverse-DNS prefix they own.

questions.question: A Tasks-extension task reaches status input_required. How does the client supply the answer?

options.text: By opening subscriptions/listen and sending the answers on that stream
tasks/update with the taskId and inputResponses
By retrying the original tools/call with inputResponses and requestState
By calling tasks/result with the answers attached

questions.explanation: This is the classic trap: core MRTR answers by retrying the original request, but the Tasks extension answers with tasks/update against the taskId. tasks/result does not exist in the redesigned extension.

questions.question: Who decides that a particular request becomes a task, and how is that possible without a per-call flag?

options.text: The server decides once per connection and applies that decision to every request that follows
The server decides per request; the client opts in once through the extension capability
The host decides, based on how long previous calls to that tool took
The client decides per call, by setting a task flag in the request params

questions.explanation: Tasks are server-directed: the client declares io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks in its per-request capabilities and must then handle either result shape, while the server chooses per request whether to return a CreateTaskResult. Returning a task to a client that did not declare support is a violation.

questions.question: How does a tool tell a host that it has an MCP App interface, and how is that interface rendered?

options.text: The tool returns an HTML content block, which the host injects into the conversation
The server exposes a resource with mimeType text/html, which the host opens in a browser tab
The tool's outputSchema declares a ui type, which the host renders natively
_meta.ui.resourceUri points at a ui:// resource, rendered in a sandboxed iframe

questions.explanation: The tool description carries _meta.ui.resourceUri pointing at a ui:// resource (text/html;profile=mcp-app). Hosts typically render it in a sandboxed iframe, and _meta.ui may also carry csp and permissions.

questions.question: An MCP App wants to call a tool in response to a button click. What does the security model say?

options.text: It calls the server directly over its own HTTP connection, using the host's token
It may call only tools exposed by the same server, without further checks
It asks the host over postMessage, and the host applies its normal consent and policy
It cannot call tools at all: apps are display-only surfaces

questions.explanation: Apps are isolated in a sandboxed iframe and communicate with the host through postMessage using a JSON-RPC dialect (ui/ methods plus shared ones like tools/call). The host controls which capabilities the app may use, and tool calls run through the host's consent path.

questions.question: You call tasks/cancel, and the next tasks/get still shows working, then completed. Is the implementation broken?

options.text: No: cancellation is cooperative, so a task may still finish before it notices
Yes: a cancelled task must report cancelled on the next tasks/get
No, but the server must then re-run the task so that the earlier result is discarded
Yes: tasks/cancel must block until the task reaches a terminal state

questions.explanation: Cancellation is a request, not a kill switch: the server stops work where it can, and a task already past the point of no return may reach completed or failed instead. Once a terminal state is reached it does not change again.
